title: Module 2: Application Analysis and Design
description: Planning and design before building: the three design areas, the application development checklist, defining process and stakeholders, inputs/outputs, the data model, client-side vs server-side architecture, UI options, and ServiceNow design recommendations.

questions.prompt: What is the central principle motivating the analysis and design work in this module?

choices.text: Always build a prototype first and design afterward.
Design and plan before building, because reworking a built application is far more costly than changing a plan.
The user interface should be finalized before any data modeling.
Applications should be built without a checklist to stay flexible.

questions.explanation: The module's guiding idea is to plan well up front, because changing something on paper is far cheaper than reworking a built application.

questions.prompt: The module breaks application design into three areas. Which of the following are those three design areas? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Business logic
Database logic
Deployment logic
User interface

questions.explanation: Design is analyzed as business logic, database logic, and user interface. Deployment is a separate concern, not one of the three design areas.

questions.prompt: Why does the recommended design sequence put business logic and database logic before the user interface?

choices.text: Because the user interface cannot be built until security is fully applied.
Because cosmetic UI changes are comparatively cheap, while changing the underlying data model and server logic after the build is costly.
Because ServiceNow forbids designing the UI before the data model exists.
Because the UI determines which tables the database needs.

questions.explanation: The logic underneath (data model, server-side behavior) is hard and expensive to change later, while the UI is comparatively easy to adjust, so the foundational logic is settled first.

questions.prompt: According to the module, what must exist before you decide you need to build an application?

choices.text: A clear business problem to solve.
An approved budget for cloud hosting.
A finished data model diagram.
A list of required integrations.

questions.explanation: If you are not solving a business problem, you do not need an application. A clear, stated business problem is the starting point.

questions.prompt: How should the desired outcomes / definition of done for an application be written?

choices.text: As broad aspirational goals so the team has flexibility.
In clear, observable, and measurable language, agreed upon before development begins.
Only after the application is built, based on what was achieved.
As a list of tables and columns to be created.

questions.explanation: Outcomes should be observable and measurable and agreed before development, so you can test whether you succeeded and avoid discovering at the end that the wrong problem was solved.

questions.prompt: In ServiceNow, user personas defined during design largely map to which platform concept used to apply security?

choices.text: Update Sets
Roles
Client Scripts
Business Rules

questions.explanation: Personas largely equate to roles in ServiceNow, and security is generally applied to applications and their records using roles.

questions.prompt: What is the recommendation regarding the minimum roles an application should define?

choices.text: A single Admin role is sufficient for any application.
At least a User role and an Admin role.
One role per table in the application.
No application-specific roles; reuse the global admin role only.

questions.explanation: It is recommended that every application have at least a User role and an Admin role.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are valid output methods to consider when defining a process? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Dashboards
Reports
Email notifications
Access Control Lists

questions.explanation: Outputs can take the form of dashboards, reports, and email. ACLs are a security mechanism, not an output method.

questions.prompt: When planning inputs, what does the "coalesce" consideration address?

choices.text: How frequently the data is received.
What makes a record unique, so duplicate data can be matched and updated rather than re-inserted.
Which role is allowed to submit the input.
The visual layout of the input form.

questions.explanation: Coalesce concerns what makes data unique, which is how the platform decides whether incoming data matches an existing record (to avoid duplicates) versus creating a new one.

questions.prompt: Which input method is suggested for loading data that arrives as a spreadsheet file?

choices.text: A custom Service Portal widget
An Import Set
A Business Rule
A Scheduled Report

questions.explanation: Spreadsheet input is retrieved via an Import Set.

questions.prompt: What does a data model describe?

choices.text: The visual theme and branding of the application.
The data the application reads from and writes to the database, and how it is stored.
The sequence of automated email notifications.
The roles assigned to each persona.

questions.explanation: The data model describes the data the application reads from and writes to the database and how it is stored, captured as tables, columns, and relationships.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are examples of foundation data that is shared by many different applications? (Choose 3)

choices.text: user
cmdb_ci
task
A custom application-specific table

questions.explanation: user, cmdb_ci, and task are foundation data shared by many applications. Application-specific tables are unique to a given app.

questions.prompt: To represent people in a new application without breaking existing relationships, what approach is recommended?

choices.text: Extend the user table directly so the new app inherits all user fields.
Create a custom table whose name/reference field points to the existing user table, preserving existing many-to-many relationships such as users-groups and users-roles.
Duplicate all user records into a new standalone table.
Store people as comma-separated values in a single string field.

questions.explanation: Rather than extending the user table, build a custom table that references the existing user table, so the established many-to-many relationships (users-groups, users-roles, and so on) remain intact.

questions.prompt: What is the guidance on client-side scripting in a scoped application's architecture?

choices.text: Maximize client-side scripting to reduce server load.
Keep client-side scripting to a minimum (thin client).
Client-side scripting is not allowed in scoped applications.
All logic must run client-side for performance.

questions.explanation: Client-side scripting should be kept thin, with reusable logic placed server-side.

questions.prompt: Which artifact provides a single location for reusable server-side functions, reducing maintenance effort?

choices.text: Client Script
UI Policy
Script Include
Notification

questions.explanation: Script Includes provide a single location for reusable functions, reducing maintenance and time-to-completion.

questions.prompt: When designing the user experience, which of the following are valid ways users might interact with an application? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Standard catalog item or record producer
Workspace
Portal or mobile experience
Update Set

questions.explanation: Interaction options include a standard catalog item, record producer, workspace, portal, and mobile experience. An Update Set is a deployment/configuration-transfer mechanism, not a user interaction method.

questions.prompt: Regardless of how the application is ultimately presented to users, what foundation does the course say every application starts from?

choices.text: Records, tables, and forms.
Service Portal widgets.
REST integrations.
Scheduled reports.

questions.explanation: Whatever UI is layered on top, the foundation is always records, tables, and forms.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are ServiceNow design recommendations highlighted in this module? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Develop private-scoped applications.
Give every process its own scope.
Track development tasks.
Put all logic in the global scope for easier sharing.

questions.explanation: The recommendations are to develop private-scoped applications, give every process its own scope, follow delegated development practices, and track development tasks. Defaulting everything to global scope contradicts this guidance.

questions.prompt: Why is producing a flowchart during the design phase especially valuable in ServiceNow?

choices.text: It is required before any table can be created.
It maps nicely onto automation tools such as Flow Designer when it is time to build workflows.
It automatically generates the application's ACLs.
It replaces the need for a data model.

questions.explanation: A detailed process flowchart lends itself directly to automation tools like Flow Designer, making the later build easier.

questions.prompt: What does the Application Development Checklist represent in this course?

choices.text: A legally mandated sequence every ServiceNow app must follow exactly.
A foundational roadmap and starting point, which teams may adapt with their own wording and order.
A list of release features delivered in the latest version.
A set of ACL rules applied automatically at deployment.

questions.explanation: The checklist is a good foundation and roadmap, not a rigid law; your own checklist need not use the same exact words or order.

questions.prompt: An application administrator will need a way to adjust application settings after go-live without code changes. What should the developer do about this?

choices.text: Nothing; settings can always be added instantly at the end of development.
Plan for it during design, for example by including a properties/options module so settings are configurable.
Hard-code all settings and require a new deployment to change them.
Store settings only in client-side scripts.

questions.explanation: Conveniences like a properties module for configurable settings must be planned for during design; they cannot simply be snapped into place at the end of the development cycle.
